elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Subparagraph 18.8: "Teleglobe USA Inc. (the \"Customer\") may terminate its participation in this Agreement for convenience at any time". "Terminate its participation" is the exit mechanic this multi-party agreement uses in 18.1, so the grant is the document's functional equivalent of terminating the Agreement as to us; there are no Order Forms in this construction/consortium structure, so the disjunctive alternative is unnecessary."},{"element":"Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.","level":"preferred","status":"met","evidence":"18.8: \"by giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the other Parties\" — 30 days, in writing, and no other precondition (no Management Committee approval, no unanimous consent, no cure or fee gate).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: 18.8 requires "not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice"; the right is unconditional ("at any time"), so it is a true convenience election and not gated by 18.2's unanimity requirement.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.8: "the other Parties shall refund to the Customer, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by it for the period after the effective date of such termination." "Pro rata" is express (not merely inferred from a post-termination period), the payer is the counterparty side, and "any amounts prepaid" necessarily includes prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained 18.1 lets "any Party ... terminate its participation ... at the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter" on one year's notice — the effective date is expressly tied to term end or later, not mid-term; retained 18.2 permits mid-term termination only "by agreement in writing of all the Parties," which requires our own consent. No counterparty unilateral mid-term convenience right exists, and 18.8 is expressed as our right alone ("the Customer may"), so it does not create one.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted notice period is thirty (30) days, which is outside the 60–90 day band. This is a more favourable (preferred-level) term rather than a defect; the fallback band is simply not the level being pursued.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: 18.8 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, instalment or contingent payment on our exit, and no such charge is introduced elsewhere by the edit. With no fee mechanic, the cap requirement is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: 18.1 confines a Party's unilateral exit to "the end of the Initial Period or any time thereafter"; during the 25-year Initial Period, 18.2 requires unanimous written agreement. Termination effect is expressly anchored to term end, so this is not a mere notice-based right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: 18.1 requires "not less than one (1) year's prior notice ... in writing," which exceeds the 90-day floor.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language — a 30-day, unconditional Customer convenience exit with an express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts (new 18.8), and retained 18.1/18.2 already deny the counterparty Parties any unilateral mid-term convenience exit (term-end-or-later only, on one year's notice).

Finding status "deviation" is correct: before the edit there was no Customer convenience right at all in a 25-year committed term, which is walk-away territory under the rule, so a redline was warranted rather than a fallback acceptance.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion, no deletions, no rewriting of the favourable counterparty-side constraints in 18.1/18.2, and no model-language extras (no survival tail, no "in whole or in part" surplus, no procedures or damages add-ons). Keying the new right to "terminate its participation" mirrors the document's own mechanic instead of introducing an alien construct.

Intent preserved: 18.5 (no capital-cost credit) and 18.7 (continuing liability tail) are expressly keyed to Subparagraph 18.1 and are untouched, so placing the new right in 18.8 leaves no textual contradiction, dangling cross-reference or undefined term; the newly defined "Customer" is used only within 18.8 and matches the signatory block at p0322.

Watch item, not a defect: the refund reaches "any amounts prepaid" rather than "prepaid fees". That is broader in our favour and satisfies the element, but because it is not keyed to 18.1 it could be read to sweep in prepaid capital contributions that 18.5 would deny on an 18.1 exit; if the counterparty presses, fall back to "any fees or other amounts prepaid by it" rather than conceding the notice period or the pro-rata basis.

Optional hardening if the counterparty argues 18.8 is ambiguous as to consortium consents: add "notwithstanding Subparagraph 18.2" is unnecessary — 18.2 addresses termination of the whole Agreement, not a single Party's participation — but confirming that no Management Committee determination is required would remove any argument that 18.7's "Unless the Management Committee shall otherwise determine" opener bears on the new right.
